subject: spaceGalley
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: spaceship galley kitchen.
Style: Alien (1979) Nostromo.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static Nostromo-style galley kitchen prop built from THREE geometries via b.part calls, aiming for a compact but detailed module without needing a joint rig.

Specifically I'm laying out dimensions for a floor slab, back wall counter run, upper cabinets, stove, sink, coffee machine, hanging rack, mess table with stools, overhead pipes, and glowing monitors, all within the Nostromo's dirty beige/amber/teal-green palette, while planning helper functions for boxes and cylinders and keeping rivet details under the part budget.

I'll add a left wall with a bulkhead hatch door featuring a frame and wheel handle, plus ceiling pipes with flange bands and a glowing strip light overhead. Then I'm building a counter run of steel base cabinets with a slab top, toe kick, and doors with handles and drawer details.

Now I'm placing kitchen fixtures: a stove with four burner rings (one glowing orange) and a pot with lid, a sink with faucet and taps, and a coffee machine with a glass pot and glow lights. I'm also planning upper cabinets with doors and latches, a gap for a glowing wall-mounted CRT monitor, and a tapered hood frustum over the stove.

I'm adding a hanging utensil rail under the cabinets with a ladle, spatula, and pans, plus a central table with a slab top, pedestal legs, and four mounted stools, topped with mugs, a food tray, and a bottle. I'm also starting on a fridge or locker unit to the right.

Working out layout coordinates...

I'm reconsidering the layout to avoid collisions—moving the coffee machine to the table end instead of under cabinet B, and thinking about whether a right-side wall or hatch is needed to balance the tall unit on the left.

I'm placing a towel rail below the monitor on the back wall, adjusting faucet height and spout position so the hanging items clear the counter edge properly. Now I'm setting up helper functions for boxes and cylinders to start building the geometry in code.

I'm planning the screen texture as an SVG with a dark green background and glowing monospace readout text, plus a separate warning plaque decal with yellow and black styling for added detail.

Then I'm sketching out helper logic for hazard stripe boxes and a rivet row using cheap low-poly spheres repeated around a hundred times for texture without cost. For the ceiling, I'm skipping a full slab and instead adding overhead light strips and pipe beams near the top so the view isn't blocked, then moving into writing the actual wall and room dimensions in code.

Laying out 5 cabinet doors across the counter span with evenly spaced centers, plus small handle boxes for each. I'm putting a glowing oven window near the stove position with an orange indicator glow to suggest it's on.

Now building the hob top: a black plate with four burner rings, one lit up with a glowing red-orange torus, plus a steel pot with lid and handle sitting on it. For the sink, I'm adding a recessed dark basin, a faucet post, and a horizontal spout extending toward the basin.

Next I'm placing the coffee machine, upper cabinet, and range hood with its taper and ceiling duct, then adding a tall cabinet unit with a front door panel on the left side of the kitchen.

Now I'm building the right wall with its circular hatch door, including the frame, rim torus, and wheel spokes positioned at the correct height and depth.

I'm also positioning the central table with its pedestal legs and surrounding stools, adjusting the deck depth to fit everything comfortably in the scene.

Adding orange vinyl seat details and a disc base, plus table props like a sectioned tray, mugs with handles, a bottle, and a noodle bowl. I'm also laying out overhead pipework along the x-axis with flanges, a valve wheel, and a glowing ceiling light panel above the table.

Now I'm detailing the back wall: horizontal seams, a steel backsplash strip, vertical panel seams, and a colored stripe band for that Nostromo aesthetic. I'm adding rows of rivets across the wall and considering a warning plaque texture near the hatch.

I'll place a "GALLEY / DECK C" sign above the tall unit at the back wall, offset slightly from the wall surface, and finish up with monospace SVG text for the labels before exporting the module.
